Elena sent the HorizonCare questionnaire this morning. They've asked for a mapped response to NIST AI RMF and EU AI Act, plus evidence by EOD 5/4 PT. I'm assigning quick owners so we can turn this around:

- Marissa: Assurance matrix and evidence files (SOC2 snapshot, penetration test summary, KMS/HSM attestation).

A few technical talking points to include in the responses (short bullets you can copy):
- Continuous regression: our regression harness runs nightly against production-sampled prompts and scheduled evaluation suites (unit/regression/manual evals). We store baseline outputs and compute delta metrics (ROUGE/EM/clinically relevant task-specific F1) with automated alerts on drift/regression.
- Traceability: full request-level audit logs (request id -> model version, prompt, input hash, output hash, routing decision, KV-cache snapshot id) retained per customer policy (default 90 days, configurable up to 7 years on Private).
- Explainability & provenance: prediction metadata includes top-k token probabilities, sampling seeds, and model config; we provide structured output options to produce consistent explainability metadata for downstream validation.
- Rollouts: canary -> gradual rollout -> A/B -> full; automatic rollback triggers on latency or quality regressions (user-defined thresholds).
- Data residency: Private with customer-managed VPC ensures no egress; Dedicated supports region pinning for compliance.

I'll assemble the files; please add final sentences where you own. We will attach: redwood-assurance-matrix-2026.xlsx, regression-harness-overview.pdf, evidence-soc2-snapshot-2026.pdf.

Vanessa

Elena —

Please find our response attached and summarized below. We prepared a short evidence bundle and an appendix with technical diagrams and the evaluation/regression approach. Given the clinical context, we've focused the answers on traceability, reproducibility, and operational controls that minimize model drift and provide forensic evidence for decisions.

Attachments: redwood-assurance-matrix-2026.xlsx; regression-harness-overview.pdf; evidence-soc2-snapshot-2026.pdf

Executive summary (copied into the questionnaire fields):
- NIST AI RMF: Redwood maps NIST core functions (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage, and Protect) to product features and operational processes. Examples:
  - Govern: versioned model registry, documented ownership for model artifacts, and policy-driven rollout gates.
  - Map: risk tagging at model onboarding (use-case + data sensitivity), automated threat modelling for high-risk models.
  - Measure: continuous metrics (quality, fairness proxies, robustness), sampled human-in-the-loop review triggered on drift or safety signals.
  - Manage: canary and staged rollouts, automated rollback on regression, and traceable change logs.
  - Protect: customer-controlled encryption keys (KMS/HSM), network isolation (Private), and audit logging.

- EU AI Act positioning: HorizonCare's clinical decision workflows are high-concern. Our standard controls for high-risk deployments include: documented conformity assessment artifacts; artifact-level traceability (model training data lineage at a high level); pre-deployment evaluation suites with minimum pass thresholds; and deployment controls (Private/Dedicated modes, model pinning, region lock). We'll include a suggested conformity checklist in the matrix.

- Evaluation & regression approach (detailed in regression-harness-overview.pdf):
  - Continuous large-scale regression harness that executes nightly against a production-sampled cohort (configurable sampling rate). Each run compares new model outputs to pinned baselines across multiple evaluation suites: unit tests, domain-specific clinical metrics, adversarial perturbations, and human-graded cohorts for high-impact prompts.
  - Metrics and thresholds: we compute delta metrics with confidence intervals; for clinically-sensitive tasks we surface primary clinical-readout metrics (e.g., diagnostic suggestion F1, false-positive rate) and block rollout if thresholds are exceeded.
  - Human-in-the-loop sampling: failed items are triaged with annotation workflows; findings feed back into model improvement pipelines and into the governance evidence log.
  - Reproducibility & trace data: each evaluation includes model binary id, seeds, tokenizer version, kernel/quantization profile, and exact hardware target to ensure reproducible runs.

- Auditability: per-request audit logs with immutable IDs, signed by customer-managed keys where required. Logs include routing decisions (why a request used a specific model variant), batching decisions affecting latency, and fallback events. Default retention 90 days; available extension to 7 years on Private deployments.

- Security & evidence: SOC2 type II snapshot and pen-test summary included. We also provide KMS/HSM integration docs and a suggested controls map for KPMG review.

Next steps / ask: Please confirm if KPMG prefers the attached evidence as-is, or if you'd like a short review call (we can do 30 minutes Wed 5/6). We can also prepare a tailored SOC2+ controls mapping for HorizonCare's control set if needed.

Best regards,
Dylan Brooks
Account Lead, Healthcare
Redwood Inference
